entries.opening: There is no direct import, but there is a way to do it with an automation tool.

steps.text: Blotato has no native CSV import for the content calendar. You cannot upload a spreadsheet of captions, links, and dates directly in the web app.

cite.quote: Blotato has no native CSV import for the content calendar. You cannot upload a spreadsheet of captions, links, and dates directly in the web app.

steps.text: To bulk-schedule from a spreadsheet, use the Blotato API with an automation tool.

cite.quote: To bulk-schedule a month of posts from a spreadsheet, use the Blotato API with an automation tool:

steps.text: Put your captions, media URLs, and dates in a Google Sheet or Airtable.

cite.quote: Put your captions, media URLs, and dates in a Google Sheet or Airtable

steps.text: In n8n or Make, add a Google Sheets (or Airtable) trigger to read each row, then map each row into the Blotato Publish Post node.

cite.quote: In n8n or Make, add a Google Sheets (or Airtable) trigger to read each row 3. Map each row into the Blotato Publish Post node

steps.text: Set scheduledTime on each row for exact dates, or set useNextFreeSlot to true to fill your calendar slots automatically.

cite.quote: Set scheduledTime per row for exact dates, or useNextFreeSlot: true to fill your calendar slots automatically

entries.next: Put your posts in a Google Sheet or Airtable, then build the n8n or Make workflow with the trigger, the Publish Post node, and scheduledTime or useNextFreeSlot.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when your rows show up as scheduled posts in your Blotato calendar.

entries.opening: There is no approval link in the web app, but there are two ways to get a review step.

steps.text: Blotato does not have a built-in approval-link feature in the web app.

steps.text: In the web app, create your post and schedule it for a future time, then review all scheduled posts in Posts > Scheduled.

steps.text: To pause a post for edits, open the three-dot menu and choose Move to Drafts. Publish or reschedule once you are satisfied.

steps.text: To connect an account, go to Accounts and click Connect account, then the platform. For a second account on the same platform, look for the button with 3 dots to switch accounts and select the correct one.

cite.quote: To connect an account, go to Accounts and click the "Connect account > [Platform]" button. If you're connecting a second account for the same platform, look for a button with 3 dots to switch between accounts and select the correct one.

steps.text: If that does not work, or it keeps logging into the wrong account, use an incognito browser as a last resort.

entries.opening: Blotato logs you in with a code sent to your email, and that is where the trouble usually is.

steps.text: Blotato uses magic link authentication, so there is no password.

cite.quote: Blotato uses magic link authentication, so there is no password.

steps.text: Your email must match your account email exactly, in all lowercase.

cite.quote: Check the spelling of your email first: it must match your account email exactly, in all lowercase.

steps.text: Check your spam and junk folders for the code.

cite.quote: Check your spam and junk folders.

steps.text: With a work email, corporate mail filters are the most common cause of a missing code.

cite.quote: Corporate mail filters are the most common cause -- they silently block the verification email.

steps.text: If the code still does not arrive, ask in the support chat to temporarily switch your account email to a personal address.

entries.opening: An uploaded file still gets a web address behind the scenes, so a fetch error is worth checking step by step.

steps.text: A local upload still becomes a hosted media URL for publishing, and a fetch or parsing error does not, by itself, prove a corrupt file or a broken stored link.

cite.quote: A local upload still becomes a hosted media URL for publishing. A fetch or parsing error does not, by itself, prove a corrupt file or invalid stored reference.

steps.text: Write down the exact error and the failed post ID.

cite.quote: Record the exact error and failed post ID.

steps.text: Confirm the upload finished and the media is accessible.

cite.quote: Confirm the upload finished and the resulting media is accessible.

steps.text: Check the file's container, codecs, dimensions, duration, and size against the destination's media requirements. A .mp4 filename alone is not proof of its format.

cite.quote: Check the file's container, codecs, dimensions, duration, and size against the destination's media requirements. A .mp4 filename alone is not proof of its format.

steps.text: If the upload failed or its stored link is unusable, upload the valid file again and replace the failed draft's attachment, then check whether any destination already published before you schedule the replacement. If the media is accessible and meets the requirements, send support the error and post ID instead of repeating uploads.

cite.quote: If the upload failed or its stored URL is unusable, upload the valid source file again and replace the failed draft's attachment. 5. Verify whether any destination already published before scheduling a replacement. If the media is accessible and meets the requirements, send support the error and post ID for log inspection instead of repeating uploads.

entries.next: Write down the exact error and the failed post ID, then check the file against the destination's media requirements.
entries.proof: Still open: if the media is accessible and meets the requirements, support needs the exact error and post ID to look at the logs.
